newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris mayor probed for misuse of public funds.
newsitem.headline: Paris mayor probed for misuse of public funds.

text.p: The Gaullist mayor of Paris, Jean Tiberi, said in an interview published on Thursday that he, as well as his wife, was being formally investigated on suspicion of misusing public funds.
Tiberi, who succeeded President Jacque Chirac as Paris mayor in 1995, said he was innocent, indicating he would not resign.
"I have just received notice that I am being placed under investigation...in the case regarding my wife," he told the pro-government daily Le Figaro.
"As I have nothing to reproach myself with, nor does my wife, I am sure law will prevail," he said.

The case came as a new blow to the ruling Gaullist RPR party whose personnel chief Louise-Yvonne Casetta is being probed in a separate sleaze case in connection with alleged illicit funding of the party.
Tiberi's wife Xaviere was placed under investigation last December on suspicion of misusing public funds.

Investigators say they suspect her of receiving 200,000 francs ($40,000) from a regional elected council for a 36-page report largely copied out of a book, and of having the money paid into a joint bank account she holds with her husband.
Xavier Dugoin, Gaullist president of the Essone regional authority outside Paris, is also being investigated for allegedly paying the sum to Mrs Tiberi.
Dugoin was reported to have told investigators that Tiberi himself decided the amount to be paid to his wife.

The case led to a much-publicised episode in which Gaullist Justice Minister Jacques Toubon acknowledged ordering a helicopter to be chartered to track down a magistrate holidaying in Nepal, in an effort to head off the probe of Mrs Tiberi, which was being pursued in the magistrate's absence by an independent-minded deputy.
